query: Two Pale Heads {flag(dumont_reunited): The photographer is herding the year onto the great hall steps. At the end of a row, two pale heads lean together, Kael and Ilse, who was raised to open the door he refused. Kael sees you and moves up, which leaves a space between them and the edge.|The photographer is herding the year onto the great hall steps. At the end of a row Kael stands beside a space nobody is allowed to fill. Ilse should be in it. The man in grey took her north, and no letter has come.} {flag(dumont_reunited): Squeeze into the photograph with them|Leave the space empty with him} You squeeze in beside them, and Ilse elbows you, and Kael, for once, laughs out loud just as the shutter goes. It's the only photograph of the three of you, and it hangs in two houses for the rest of your lives. You stand at the edge of the space, so it stays a space, and Kael's hand finds your shoulder for a moment. In the photograph there's a gap in the row the size of a girl in white furs. {flag(dumont_reunited): Take the photograph yourself|Talk Kael into closing the gap} You take the camera from the photographer and make them stand still for once. Two Dumonts, squinting at the sun, in nobody's photograph but yours. "She'd hate being a gap," you tell him, and he almost smiles, and moves up. In the photograph the row closes. Neither of you forgets why it was open.
